newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Elec focusing on system LSIs.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Elec focusing on system LSIs.

text.p: Mitsubishi Electric Corp said on Friday its medium-term business strategy will focus on system LSI chips, aiming to boost sales of the chips to 40 billion yen in the fiscal year starting April 1998.

The plan is part of Mitsubishi's strategy to lessen its dependence on the volatile dynamic random access memory (DRAM) business and expand areas that promise steady profits, Mitsubishi's senior managing director Shoji Hirabayashi said.
"We also hope to differentiate ourselves from U.S. and South Korean competitors with system LSIs, in which we have a competitive edge," Hirabayashi told a news conference.
System LSIs integrate memory and logic on a single chip, enabling production of smaller chips with high speed and low power consumption.
Applications include graphics and network computers, handy phones, digital still cameras and digital televisions.

Mitsubishi's technology in large-volume memory chips, logic chips, such as micro-controllers and ASICs (application-specific integrated circuits), and home electronics, making it advantageous in the system LSI business, Hirabayashi said.
Mitsubishi expects its total semiconductor sales to grow to 630 billion yen in the 1998/99 year ending on March 31, 1999, up from an estimated 530 billion yen the previous year.
Mitsubishi currently depends on DRAMs for 38 percent of its semiconductor sales but aims to lower the ratio to around 30 percent in the 2000/2001 year, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
